items.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued October 16 at 3:47PM EDT until October 20 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
items.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves 10 to
14 feet expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood
Watch, one to two feet of inundation above ground level
possible in low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways near high tide starting on Sunday, and continuing
into Monday and potentially through mid week.

* WHERE...Virginia Beach.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from noon Saturday to 6 PM
EDT Monday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Sunday afternoon
through Tuesday morning. Coastal Flooding and high surf may
continue into mid week.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.
items.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 16 at 1:11PM EDT until October 17 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
items.description:
* WHAT...North to northeast winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 50
mph expected.

* WHERE...In North Carolina, Eastern Currituck County. In Virginia,
Virginia Beach.

* WHEN...From noon Saturday to 8 PM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

items.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 16 at 2:39PM EDT until October 17 at 7:00AM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Small Craft Advisory, northwest winds 15 to 25 kt
with gusts up to 30 kt and seas 2 to 4 ft expected. For the Gale
Warning, north winds 30 to 40 kt with a few gusts up to 50 kt
and seas 11 to 16 ft expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Waters from Cape Charles Light to Virginia-
North Carolina border out 20 NM and Coastal waters from NC VA
border to Currituck Beach Light NC out 20 NM.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, from 10 PM this evening
to 7 AM EDT Saturday. For the Gale Warning, from 7 AM Saturday
to 6 AM EDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
items.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for hazardous conditions.
